# Layer 1: portfolio, imports and the investment ledger

**MP / Mypaisaa Prediction · PH-01 · Draft 0.1 for review · 1 November 2026**  
**Not implemented. End-to-end requirements, UX and architecture selection remain unapproved.**

[Planning index]({{page:NEW-PLANNING-INDEX}}) · [Phased plan]({{page:NEW-PHASED-PLAN}}) · [Architecture]({{page:NEW-ARCHITECTURE}}) · [Technology matrix]({{page:NEW-TECH-STACK}}) · [Story contracts]({{page:NEW-PORTFOLIO-IMPORT}}) · [Entity contracts]({{page:NEW-PORTFOLIO-IMPORT}}) · [Worked examples]({{page:NEW-PORTFOLIO-IMPORT}})

## 1. Outcome, authority and boundaries

Give the owner a trustworthy investment record: what is held, in which account and listing, what happened, where each fact came from, which figures can be computed, and what remains unknown. Imports must be reviewable, reproducible, idempotent and reversible through an auditable correction process. A statement becoming available is not the same as a financial change being applied.

DEC-001–041 in the [decision register](https://duttaarun2015.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/mypaisaapr/pages/4981241) are the current owner decisions. This layer expands them into proposed contracts and acceptance criteria; it does not approve the unasked defaults. DEC-041 makes synthetic local/dev work the current phase. Actual holdings and broker screenshots/PDFs will arrive progressively later and are not a prerequisite for this specification.

The application is independent of mypaisa-agent. It owns its own investment accounts, source documents, ledger, observations and conversations. No shared production ledger or migration is assumed. It records historical investment events and suggestions; it never executes a trade or requests broker trading credentials.

Initial analysis covers UK/US/India equities and ETFs, with versioned extension points for further markets and instruments. Account/wrapper context and the captured Indian CAS/fund-import requirements are retained as planned contracts; supported institution/layout families must be agreed and tested. A new unsupported instrument type, accounting action or jurisdiction policy requires a compatible implementation and evidence, not arbitrary unvalidated configuration.

**Present evidence:** health/sample SSE starter; validated synthetic market/ledger packs for 30 real instrument IDs; generic synthetic PDF/raster companions and expected extraction records. **Absent:** a production import API, parser/OCR service, financial repository, transaction commit engine, Cognito implementation or portfolio UI. Planning/story status cannot certify those features.

## 2. Journeys and first-version input coverage

The same durable workflow serves PWA, native Apple clients and contextual chat. A chat attachment is an entry point to the import process, not a separate financial authority. Human confirmation occurs through an authenticated owner flow; the document, model and research agent cannot confirm on the owner's behalf.

| Journey | Proposed behaviour | Evidence needed before release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Structured history | CSV and a versioned Excel workbook map accounts, holdings, transactions and valuations; preview row-level results before applying | Generic templates, field/date/currency errors, duplicate/reprocess and large-history tests |
| PDF statement | Supported text layouts use code extraction; unsupported layouts enter a bounded assisted draft/review flow | Generic synthetic foundation plus qualified target broker/CAS families; incomplete/rotated/encrypted/malformed tests |
| Screenshot | Extract visible facts with page/image regions, source timestamp and uncertainty; distinguish snapshot from dated history | Current clean raster fixtures plus later cropped/blurred/photographed and actual sample qualification |
| Manual/guided entry | Ask only missing fields, preserve user wording, validate units/dates, then show the same review card | Resume/cancel/expired/stale/error/privacy/accessibility flows |
| Factsheet/research document | Resolve an instrument or research candidate; ask for owner quantity/history separately | A factsheet never becomes evidence of owner quantity or acquisition cost |
| Later history/backfill | Compare new events with existing observations/history and propose a rebase/correction | No double application of an opening position and its historical transactions |
| Correct or reverse | Show dependent effects, changed totals and affected evidence before a separately approved correction | Original events/approval and issued forecast versions remain inspectable |

All five input methods are required in the first version (DEC-005/039). This is not universal broker-format support. A supported-layout register records format/version, expected fields, known limitations and test evidence; an unqualified layout is labelled unsupported or review-required. Existing PDF/PNG companions do not constitute an OCR evaluation, and Excel-layout fixtures remain work to plan. Actual sample collection is deferred, not silently removed from later real-import qualification.

Suggested workbook sheets follow the captured reference intent: Accounts, Holdings, Transactions and Valuations. The exact template columns, type bounds and supported CAS families remain a specification choice. Ten thousand transaction rows are a useful proposed scale benchmark from the captured source; runtime, cost and response-time targets require a measured resource model rather than a promise inherited from another app.

## 3. Domain contracts and identity

The [structured contracts]({{page:NEW-PORTFOLIO-IMPORT}}) describe field families and invariants; they are draft design material, not deployed API schemas or migrations.

A security/share class, a listing and a provider symbol are different identities. A security can have multiple venue/currency listings. ISIN alone is not permission to combine them. The fixture key `XLON:CNX1` is a real public listing example and does not identify the owner's still-unconfirmed ETF. Provider aliases and ticker changes are effective-dated; a mapping revision never silently renames old events.

Accounts carry owner, environment, institution alias, country, kind and settlement currency context. US brokerage, UK wrapper and Indian demat/folio information is source-backed metadata. No legal/tax treatment is inferred from a label. Multi-currency accounts and later asset types fit versioned contracts; there is no household/member-sharing requirement in this owner-only app.

Every record belongs to the server-authorized owner/environment namespace. Client strings and a PDF's text cannot select a production dataset or bypass authorization. Records may store minimized protected account-reference tokens; full sensitive originals, where necessary, remain in private encrypted evidence storage. This does not mean retained PDFs contain no personal information.

| Entity | Purpose | Selected invariant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ScopeEnvelope | Authoritative namespace and version metadata | Every account/document/draft/event/read is scoped and authorized server-side. |
| Money | A signed decimal amount with an explicit ISO currency | No binary float, NaN, infinity or implicit currency. |
| InstrumentListing | Security/share-class identity and venue-specific quote contract | ISIN alone does not uniquely identify a listing or trading currency. |
| InvestmentAccount | An owner-scoped investment account and context | No broker trading credentials or execution authority. |
| SourceDocument | Original bytes and lifecycle/provenance | Private encrypted originals precede extraction; failed/rejected uploads remain observable. |
| ExtractionCandidate | Untrusted, non-authoritative proposed values | No tools or financial writes in document extraction. |
| ImportDraft | An immutable reviewable import revision | Any edit, mapping change, subset choice or reprocess changes the review hash. |
| OwnerApproval | A narrow server-verified approval intent | Approval binds the exact payload/scope/version; a chat yes is not an unscoped reusable credential. |
| LedgerEvent | A recorded economic event, never a trade instruction | Events are append-only; corrections produce linked new events. |
| CommitReceipt | A durable idempotent visibility decision | Exactly one logical application under retries, not exactly-once message delivery. |
| PositionObservation | A dated holding/valuation report with explicit sufficiency | A holdings snapshot is not evidence of a purchase date or external cash flow. |
| ReconciliationResult | Differences and owner disposition | No unexplained plug event or silent source-value replacement. |
| MetricResult | A value with eligibility, scope and method | Zero return and unavailable return are different. |
| AuditEvidence | Durable change/source/approval lineage | No sampling of required business audit/forecast lineage. |
| DomainNotification | Resumable progress about durable state | SSE/notifications are advisory; durable authenticated reads establish the truth. |

Identifiers are opaque application IDs except explicitly typed external identifiers. Money, quantities, dates, source locations and versions are explicit. Missing data is represented independently per field; a row does not become complete because some fields were extracted confidently.

## 4. Financial semantics: no invented history or unit conversions

Use decimal strings at contract boundaries and deterministic decimal arithmetic in code. Reject non-finite values, malformed literals, ambiguous currencies and unsupported precision; retain the raw literal for review. Preserve source-booked net cash amounts separately from calculated gross/fee components. A missing fee is not automatically zero. Precision, rounding and reconciliation tolerances remain L1-Q01. Python's Decimal supports exact decimal representation and configurable arithmetic/rounding; that capability does not choose our policy automatically. [Python Decimal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/decimal.html)

GBP is the default portfolio presentation with local-currency detail (DEC-029). A native GBX quote must be converted exactly once to GBP before a GBP ledger value is computed; a source price already denominated in GBP is not converted again. Store effective/trade date, settlement date, source observation/availability time and recorded time separately when known. A date-only record retains its precision and relevant calendar context; do not invent a precise time. Same-day economic ordering comes from declared source sequence/action links or is reviewed when it affects replay. A timezone conversion does not change the original economic date.

Execution FX belongs to the booked transaction. Valuation FX belongs to a dated permitted reference series. Neither can silently replace the other. Retain original amount/currency, received amount/currency, fees, rate direction and provenance. A reference estimate may be offered in a preview, labelled as estimated; it is not evidence of the amount credited. Do not automatically add ECB or another provider merely because the source app used it. Current selected provider rights/coverage must be verified before live use.

| --- | --- | --- |
| External deposit/withdrawal | Signed cash in its currency; no invented units | External at the chosen account/portfolio boundary when verified |
| Buy/sell record | Signed units and booked net cash; gross/fees retained separately | Internal portfolio investment activity, not a broker order |
| Dividend/interest/withholding | Source-supported gross, net and deductions | Retained portfolio income is internal; instrument-level performance has its own defined cash-flow boundary |
| Reinvestment | Linked income and purchase legs/events | Avoid a duplicated external contribution or duplicated dividend return |
| Transfer | Matched linked outgoing/incoming legs and in-transit state | Internal at whole-portfolio scope, potentially external at account scope; an unmatched side remains unresolved |

| Split/reverse split | Quantity ratio and linked action/date; preserve economic cost basis | Fractional entitlement/cash-in-lieu needs explicit evidence; no fictitious gain |

| Correction/reversal | New linked events and a new projection revision | Never rewrite the original transaction, source or earlier forecast input |

A negative position/cash figure is not silently discarded or rounded into validity: preserve it as an exception, determine settled/unsettled semantics and block unsupported dependent calculations. ## 5. Sources, extraction and normalization

The source lifecycle is received → quarantined → validated or validation_failed → extracting → extracted or extraction_failed, with independent retention/deletion status. Check actual bytes, size, media signature, checksum and relevant archive/page/pixel/runtime limits. File names and Content-Type are hints, not authority. Bound decompression, embedded links, workbook formulas/macros and resource usage. A spreadsheet is data, never an executable instruction sheet.

Retain the original immutable document version and received/processing provenance. Derived extraction is separately versioned. A processing rejection, duplicate or crash still leaves a durable outcome; neither S3 success nor an LLM response means that financial records changed. S3 notification delivery can repeat; intake/workers need idempotent state transitions and orphan reconciliation. [S3 event notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EventNotifications.html)

Code parses supported structures. The bounded document/image extractor has no tools, no ledger write authority and no provider credentials in its context. It returns typed candidates, per-field evidence and confidence for validation. Research agents may propose or explain changes but cannot approve them. Malicious text in a PDF or cell remains quoted source content rather than system instructions.

Protected-file support requires an approved secure local unlocking flow. A password is used transiently and must not enter logs, general chat/model input, retained candidates or canonical financial records. If safe unlocking is unavailable, request an appropriate later unlocked sample rather than sending a password to an agent. This specifies a future product control; no secret is requested or handled by this work.

Each extracted field links to document checksum/version, parser or model/prompt/schema version, raw literal, normalized value, confidence, validation result and source locator. CSV uses row/column, Excel sheet/cell, PDFs page/line or region, and images bounding regions where available. Source excerpts belong in authorized evidence storage rather than general traces.

## 6. Import state and review contract

An import revision is distinct from its source document. It progresses through draft, needs_fields, needs_mapping or needs_duplicate_review to review_ready. Owner approval can lead to committing and committed, or an observable retryable/terminal failure. Cancelled work has no financial effect. Later supersession/reversal is a new approved operation.

The review card presents additions, skipped true duplicates, exclusions, blocked rows, account/listing matches, source currencies/dates, before/after quantities/cash, reconciliation differences and metric eligibility. Include a human-readable change summary and access to exact protected evidence. No hidden row drop or defaulting is permitted.

Every edit, mapping change, parser reprocess or subset selection creates a new canonical draft revision/hash. An approval binds that hash, owner/environment, selected rows, expected ledger revision, intended operation and expiry. Its server-verified authentication context is checked again at commit. A model-generated `approved:true`, document signature-looking text or old chat yes cannot substitute for that proof.

If the ledger/catalogue/mapping revision changes in a way that affects the preview, mark it stale and require a new preview/approval. Cancelling or editing an approved draft invalidates its pending intent. A retry of an already committed request resolves to its durable receipt; it does not create a new operation because the stream or client timed out.

Partial import is L1-Q03. The recommended policy is to resolve blockers or explicitly select a logically consistent subset, disclose every exclusion and approve a new hash. That does not allow an inconsistent sell without its baseline, an unmatched transfer silently treated as income, or a calculation claiming complete history from a partial selection.

## 7. Deduplication, concurrency and atomic visibility

Use three identities: identical uploaded bytes; the source row/reference; and the economic event. Their equality rules are not interchangeable. Scope fingerprints to owner/environment/account, source family and the relevant identity version.

A stable broker/source transaction reference is strongest replay evidence. Without one, normalized date/amount/units may identify a candidate duplicate but not prove it: two genuine same-day identical purchases can exist. Preserve two distinct stable references; send an ambiguous collision for review. Reprocessing another format must not bypass economic-event identity. A changed fact about an existing event is a correction proposal.

The durable business idempotency record binds the operation key to canonical payload and receipt for the retained ledger's lifecycle. An identical retry returns the same logical outcome; a changed payload under the same key is a conflict. Message delivery can repeat. Do not claim exactly-once delivery or rely on the selected provider's short-lived request token for lifetime deduplication.

**Atomicity is about visibility, not merely successful batches.** One logical commit must couple authoritative financial effects, required audit and outbox/publication obligations. For a small commit the selected store may provide a native transaction. For a large import, never independently publish each successful chunk as if the whole approved import completed.

The proposed scalable pattern is immutable staging under a fenced commit identity, bounded batches, a verified completeness/content digest, and one conditional activation decision against the expected ledger revision. Readers, projections, agents and outbox delivery must all honor the same committed visibility marker or approved versioned-generation mechanism. Failed/unfinished staging remains invisible; a reconciler can safely resume or retire it. A lock/lease design must prove that an expired or superseded worker cannot activate old work.

The physical schema, staging/replay proof and write/read cost are L1-Q08 and require an ADR/spike. DynamoDB's current transaction ceiling is 100 actions/4 MB; audit, dedup and metadata consume actions too. Its client request token lasts 10 minutes, so it is not our durable business receipt. S3 upload and the application database are separate boundaries. These constraints inform the design; they do not establish that a candidate store/algorithm is already approved. ## 8. Replay, snapshots and reconciliation

Authoritative events are append-only. Derived views can be rebuilt and cached, with their ledger generation, algorithm/policy and source revisions visible. Replaying the same committed history produces identical cash/units; a mutable cached balance is not an alternative ledger.

A snapshot can establish that five units were reported on a date while acquisition cost, date and prior cash flows remain unknown. Show supported valuation and identity facts, flag gaps and withhold unsupported measures. Do not invent a purchase at the snapshot price/date merely to make the ledger balance.

When complete history arrives, reconcile it against the observation and propose a baseline/window rebase. Owner-approved activation replaces the relevant projection basis without deleting evidence or counting opening units plus their full purchase history. Reconcile account-level completeness separately from selected-position completeness; absence of a holding from a cropped screenshot is not proof it was sold.

Reconciliation compares cash, units, fees, quote units, FX, action/date ordering, reported value and source coverage separately. Preserve both reported and derived values. Differences outside approved tolerances become explicit issues and require a source-backed resolution. No unexplained plug event, hidden basis reset or silent overwrite is allowed.

Correcting history creates linked replacement/reversal events and a new view revision, with downstream dependencies assessed first. A reversal cannot leave later events impossible. Already-issued predictions retain their original ledger/data cutoff and evidence; a restated portfolio is labelled restated and does not retroactively improve a forecast's input state.

## 9. Valuation and performance eligibility

Each metric returns value/unit, scope, as-of, method and source versions plus status/reasons. Quantity known does not imply cost basis known; cost basis known does not imply dated cash-flow history known. A valid quoted value can be shown while XIRR is unavailable. Zero return is a result, not an unavailable-data marker.

A complete portfolio valuation includes eligible positions, cash and approved unsettled receivable/payable treatment, converted using explicit dated FX. Market-price and FX freshness follow source/session calendars. A missing price/FX yields a visible partial-known value and a list of uncovered holdings/currencies; it is never a complete total with missing components filled as zero.

For investor-scope XIRR, externally contributed capital is negative, externally received/distributed cash positive, and an eligible terminal portfolio value supplies the closing value. Internal portfolio buys/sells, retained dividends, transfers and FX conversions do not become duplicate external contributions. Account and single-holding calculations use their own explicitly documented boundaries; a transfer can be external to an account while internal to the portfolio.

The proposed compatibility convention is the dated present-value root:

`sum(C_i / (1 + r)^((date_i - date_0).days / 365)) = 0`

Validate signs, dates, complete relevant history, common-currency conversion and terminal valuation. Missing, same-day-only, nonconvergent or ambiguous cases return unavailable/ambiguous with a reason rather than an arbitrary root or zero. Non-conventional cash flows can admit multiple roots; record the solver domain/method and do not treat the first Newton result as authoritative. Validate rate error separately from monetary present-value residual—an IRR is not measured “to the penny.” The 365-day compatibility definition and sign requirements follow Excel's documented XIRR; exact tolerances/solver policy remain to agree. [Microsoft XIRR](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/functions/xirr-function)

The synthetic -10,000/+11,000 over 365 days case gives 10%; the worked ambiguity case has more than one valid rate. These are numerical acceptance examples, not predictive performance. See E12. Realised gains, lot-selection and tax measures are not inferred from a generic average-cost rule; source-supported basis can be displayed, with unapproved methods unavailable (L1-Q05).

## 10. Privacy, audit, retention and agent costs

Every authoritative mutation links source, draft, owner approval, actor, commit, economic event and before/after evidence. Required business/forecast/approval lineage is durable and unsampled. Operational logs/traces/run summaries use DEC-036's 14/30/90-day retention subject to measured cost; those TTLs cannot delete the only reference needed by retained financial evidence.

Originals use the confirmed renewable 24-month archive with owner extension/deletion controls. No automatic expiry/deletion or irreversible retention lock is authorized by that duration choice. The record-class retention/deletion matrix remains L1-Q07. When content is deleted, retain only the agreed minimal tombstone/audit evidence, disclose missing source availability and ensure any backup restoration reapplies deletion before access. Do not retain sensitive content inside a supposed minimal tombstone.

Audit integrity needs an explicit threat model and protected verification/anchor policy; a hash chain alone is not tamper-proof against an actor able to rewrite the chain and its head. Acceptance includes synthetic missing/altered-event detection and distinguishes authorized appended corrections from unexplained tampering.

Recheck owner/environment on upload, extraction context, preview, commit, read, source access and worker continuation. Generic telemetry/push previews exclude raw imports, portfolio values, personal account identifiers, prompts/replies, passwords and signed links. Protected UI/evidence APIs are separate from general operator logs.

Parsing/extraction is budgeted activity. Record agent/model/token/latency/cache/retry/run attribution and estimate/reservation/final usage without double counting. Unknown or uncovered credit prevents new chargeable calls; optional work follows the £60/£75/£85 cash policy and £70-operation/£30-reserve planning envelope. A failed or budget-stopped import is observable, not reported as applied. The main app dashboard surfaces costs per environment/agent; provider billing collection stays scheduled/cached (Anthropic 6h, AWS daily), rather than a paid query per UI refresh.

- commit_id/import_id/draft_hash/idempotency_key
- expected_and_resulting_ledger_revision
- staged_batch_counts/content_digest
- status:preparing|committed|failed|cancelled
- visible_generation/receipt_time

**Invariants**

- Exactly one logical application under retries, not exactly-once message delivery.
- Readers/agents/outbox consumers exclude staged or failed work.
- Large imports must prove atomic visibility and fenced concurrency within the selected store's limits.

### PositionObservation

A dated holding/valuation report with explicit sufficiency

**Fields**

- observation_id/account/listing/as_of/source
- reported_quantity/value/cost_basis:independently optional
- coverage:complete_account|selected_positions|unknown
- history_start/history_complete/reconciliation_state
- baseline_revision/superseded_by

**Invariants**

- A holdings snapshot is not evidence of a purchase date or external cash flow.
- Later history must reconcile/rebase an observation rather than double-count it.
- A factsheet describes an instrument and does not prove owner quantity or ownership.

### ReconciliationResult

Differences and owner disposition

**Fields**

- reconciliation_id/import_or_view_version
- field/scope/as_of/source_values/derived_values
- tolerance_policy/difference/classification
- resolution/actor/approval_ref

**Invariants**

- No unexplained plug event or silent source-value replacement.
- Cash, quantity, fees, FX, units, action/date and history completeness reconcile separately.
- Unresolved material conflicts block dependent metrics/actions, not unrelated valid facts.

### MetricResult

A value with eligibility, scope and method

**Fields**

- metric/scope/account_or_portfolio_id
- as_of/ledger_and_price_and_FX_versions
- value:decimal string|null/unit
- status:available|partial|unavailable|ambiguous
- reasons/method_version/inputs/uncertainty

**Invariants**

- Zero return and unavailable return are different.
- XIRR scope/cash-flow signs/history and terminal valuation must be valid.
- Financial forecasts/metrics retain the input revision used when issued.

### AuditEvidence

Durable change/source/approval lineage

**Fields**

- audit_id/event_or_document_or_commit_ref
- actor/operation/effective_and_recorded_time
- protected_before_after_refs/reason
- previous_digest/integrity_anchor_ref:design pending
- retention/deletion_tombstone_link

**Invariants**

- No sampling of required business audit/forecast lineage.
- Hash chaining alone is not tamper-proof against an actor able to rewrite all records/anchors.
- Owner source deletion and recoverable backups must not resurrect deleted content or misrepresent evidence availability.

### DomainNotification

Resumable progress about durable state

**Fields**

- event_id/cursor/owner/environment
- event_type/resource_ref/revision
- occurred_at/safe_status_counts
- trace_or_run_ref

**Invariants**

- SSE/notifications are advisory; durable authenticated reads establish the truth.
- A disconnect never re-applies an import or supplies proof of commit.
- Generic logs/push previews exclude private document contents and portfolio values.

**Local draft · 1 November 2026 · MP planning only · End-to-end requirements and UX unapproved · Independent review not run**

This plan divides the whole standalone product into ten layers. For each layer, complete its requirements, versioned contracts, local stories, acceptance evidence and UX states before considering its implementation. Agree the complete end-to-end baseline and UX before any application implementation starts. A completed layer draft, existing synthetic pack or approved individual decision does not grant that implementation permission.

The immediate work is local planning with realistic synthetic inputs. Actual holdings, screenshots and PDFs will arrive progressively and do not block these drafts. Live activation later requires verified instrument identity, permitted source coverage, supported layouts and full-scope pricing. No dates, delivery duration, live accuracy, subscription availability or completed phase exits are promised here.

## Confirmed product scope that each layer must retain

The product owns its investment accounts, transactions, holdings, imports, XIRR/performance, watchlists, conversations and historical decisions. CSV, Excel, PDFs/statements, screenshots and manual entry/correction all belong in the first version. Support is sample-backed and layout-specific: uncertain extraction must be reviewed; “all methods” does not mean every institution's arbitrary document. A snapshot can support holdings without supplying enough history for XIRR. Missing history is disclosed and unsupported measures are withheld.

Start with UK, US and India and approximately 20–30 active instruments covering holdings plus an owner-approved balanced research list. Use real identifiers with synthetic values now. Later, resolve actual listing identity and permitted coverage before final live universe selection and costing. Yahoo Finance plus Twelve Data Grow remain the chosen source mix, subject to exact tier, licence, history, retention and cadence evidence. Formal forecasts are daily; quote/risk checks are every 30 minutes only where supported, otherwise daily analysis with visible timestamps and suppression of unsupported intraday alerts.

Retain next-trading-day, 5- and 20-trading-day forecasts, 3/6/12-month forecasts and separate assumption-based 3–5-year scenarios. Daily refresh does not shorten the target horizon or mature an outcome. Rules/statistical baseline, F1–F8, patterns, point-in-time data, event/exposure research, contribution/rebalance experiments and proof/track record all remain in scope. Retain the initial three objectives: long-term growth with downside protection, benchmark-relative opportunity and protection/improved contributions for existing holdings.

Ranked add/hold/pause/trim/rebalance suggestions show reasons, uncertainty and portfolio impact, with growth/protection/opportunity components at the confirmed 35%/40%/25% weights. Exact normalization, thresholds, action bands and sizing remain open. Eligibility and abstention precede ranking. Rules, ML and LLM-assisted evidence remain visible separately; disagreement cannot be hidden behind a single confidence score. Uncalibrated rule strength is not a price-event probability. Nothing executes a trade.

The first screen is discovery/market; holdings have a separate section and contextual chat is available. Main-dashboard costs are a launch requirement, not a later admin-only feature. Show environment/provider/agent/model/feature/service attribution, source age and unknown allocations; separate estimates from provider billing and gross use from credit/cash. The reported shared credit is counted once and remains unknown until verified. Live estimates, Anthropic billing every six hours and AWS billing daily retain upstream delay. At forecast monthly cash £60 warn, £75 reduce optional work and £85 pause new optional paid jobs; these are not a universal instant AWS stop. Refuse uncovered/unverifiable Claude calls and never add paid fallback automatically.

Identity uses Cognito managed Apple/Google/passkey sign-in with verified linking and two independent passkey paths. Originals use encrypted private S3, renewable 24-month retention and owner extension/deletion controls, with no automatic expiry deletion authorised yet. Logs/traces/run summaries have 14/30/90-day retention subject to cost; financial, forecast, approval and source audits have separate durable policies. Monthly focused recovery/audit exercises and relevant change-triggered checks remain required. These are requirements, not configured services.

## 3. Environments and AWS shape

Preferred ingredients are CloudFront, Route 53, API Gateway, Lambda, S3, DynamoDB and Cognito. Proposed scheduled/queued work uses EventBridge Scheduler and an explicit durable workflow/queue design. Account, region, names, roles and exact services remain unprovisioned. The earlier `us-east-1` suggestion is a candidate pending availability, privacy/latency and measured full-scope cost evidence.

| Ownership | Proposed separation | Cost/accounting treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local | Synthetic local fixtures, local API/tests, no cloud loading; optional API calls require later authority | Local compute separate from any real paid API usage |
| Dev | Separate prepared synthetic pack; eventually own data stores, identity config, queues, roles and deployment target | Dedicated workspace/key/tag/account attribution where available; no prod data copied by default |
| Prod | Owner's approved real imports and permitted providers after readiness gates | No dev write principal or public cache path into prod |
| Shared | Repository/contracts, domain/DNS if chosen, CI tooling and one reported organization credit pool | Report shared/unallocated explicitly; resource separation does not create a second credit grant |

Separate AWS accounts offer the strongest dev/prod boundary; a lower-cost single-account option would require independently scoped resources, keys, roles and deny tests. This trade-off needs an ADR and pricing, not just naming prefixes. No inherited MA account/region or permissions are assumed. Prefer infrastructure as code; no persistent NAT Gateway, ALB, RDS, GPU host or continuously provisioned ML endpoint is included by default. Required controls such as edge protection, customer-managed encryption keys, backup and telemetry still need explicit pricing; do not call them free because their workloads are small.

### Customer VPC and internet egress options

The [technical network appendix]({{page:NEW-ARCHITECTURE}}) compares **N0**, customer-VPC-unattached Lambda as the cost baseline candidate, with **N1**, a conditional split using two-AZ private isolated subnets, scoped SGs, route tables and S3/DynamoDB gateway endpoints only for justified private work. External Anthropic/Yahoo/Grow workers stay unattached in N1, retaining outbound HTTPS without customer NAT. Lambda's service execution and its customer-VPC ENI attachment are distinct. S3, DynamoDB, Cognito, API Gateway and CloudFront remain managed services outside the customer VPC; a VPC is not itself the owner-authorization layer.

The new [native network diagram]({{attachment:MP-NETWORK-OPTIONS}}) shows N0, the optional VPC structure and **N1-E**, a separately costed, unselected public-NAT/IGW alternative if all workers must attach. Public-subnet placement alone gives Lambda neither a public IP nor internet access. S3/DynamoDB gateway routes cannot reach Anthropic. Paid interface endpoints may be needed for actual private-job bootstrap/runtime paths; they are not assumed free or universally required. SGs do not filter DNS names, and a blanket `SourceVpce` resource deny must not silently block CloudFront OAC, unattached roles or recovery. These choices require the network ADR and full-scope cost evidence, with no approved Region/account/topology. ### Web serving mode

**Recommendation for evaluation:** a SvelteKit 3 static application shell on private S3 behind CloudFront, with all private data loaded from the authenticated API. Public shell content may be prerendered; authenticated routes use the appropriate client-side fallback and never bake holdings into build output. Service workers cache static assets by default; private/offline data policy requires explicit design and logout/cache-clearing tests. Static hosting does not execute server routes, server loads, form actions or server-side session logic. SvelteKit SSR would instead require a compatible runtime adapter and separate compute/session design. Choose static versus SSR in an ADR before implementation. The official [static adapter guide](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/adapter-static) distinguishes fully static output from dynamic rendering; [the official SvelteKit 3 announcement](https://svelte.dev/blog/sveltekit-3-is-here) confirms version 3 is available as of this evidence check.

### API and SSE: bounded transport, durable work

REST requests read/command durable state. A long import, research run or evaluation returns an accepted job reference once durable admission succeeds, and continues without requiring a connected UI. SSE delivers event IDs, status/resource references and selected chat deltas; it is a disposable observation channel. A disconnect must not discard an accepted job or cause a duplicate model call.

Current AWS documentation supports API Gateway response streaming on **REST APIs**, with proxy integration in `STREAM` mode, for up to **15 minutes**; idle timeouts and CloudFront behaviour also apply. Do not assume the cheaper HTTP API supports SSE response streaming. The exact Regional REST integration, authorizer, origin/CORS configuration and shorter application stream lifetime need a compatibility/cost experiment after implementation approval. Python FastAPI requires a compatible streaming adapter/custom runtime such as Lambda Web Adapter; an ordinary buffered ASGI Lambda adapter is insufficient. AWS warns a dropped connection need not stop billed function execution. [API Gateway streaming](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/response-transfer-mode.html), [Lambda streaming](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-response-streaming.html)

Proposed reconnect contract: authorize each connection and owner/resource subscription, emit durable monotonic cursor semantics within a declared scope, heartbeat, end before platform limits, and reconnect with backoff. Cursor expiry or a gap triggers an authenticated snapshot fetch and a new cursor. Chat deltas are provisional until the final assistant message is durably recorded. Replayed events do not repeat mutations, reservations or paid calls. Browser native `EventSource` does not provide a custom bearer-header interface; evaluate authenticated streaming `fetch` or a deliberately designed secure cookie/session gateway. Do not put long-lived tokens in stream URLs. If cookie authentication is selected, include CSRF and cookie origin policy. Stream/push delivery is never the authorisation check for the resource fetched afterwards.

Do not implement serverless fan-out using the current in-memory bus. Compare a bounded durable-event polling bridge with a separately costed managed fan-out option; polling incurs database/compute charges while open connections occupy Lambda duration. Notification bodies must be private/minimal, with read access checked again on open. API Gateway WebSockets would change the transport decision and require an ADR; they are not a hidden substitute for SSE.

## 4. Durable core and failure semantics

### Financial ledger and import visibility

All v1 methods remain: CSV, Excel, PDF/statements, screenshots and manual entry/correction. Support named sample-backed layouts plus generic templates; uncertain extraction enters review. Synthetic equivalents can exercise these flows locally now. Real source samples are not a prerequisite to preparing the plan, but actual supported layout promises remain unproven until their samples are validated.

1. Allocate a durable upload/document identity and expected constraints, then grant a bounded private upload path. Validate owner, environment, size/type/checksum and quarantine unsafe content before parser/model work.
2. Record the exact S3 version/checksum, parser/prompt/model versions, row/cell/page evidence, extraction confidence and terminal/retry state. S3 acceptance means bytes received, not transactions committed.
3. Produce a versioned import draft with deterministic normalized rows, source matching, duplicate/conflict findings and a preview hash. The owner confirms that exact preview; edits require a new preview/confirmation.
4. Commit once with persistent application idempotency and concurrency checks. Financial changes and required audit/outbox evidence must become visible together. Holdings/cash/XIRR derive only from committed ledger events; reversals/corrections append events with reasons and prior links.
5. Reconcile orphan objects, missing metadata, duplicate storage callbacks and jobs interrupted between services. Owner-visible failed/pending states remain investigable.

**DynamoDB fit gate:** explicitly design access patterns, immutable event keys, uniqueness/duplicate indexes, concurrency and balance precision before choosing a schema. Financial amounts use defined decimal/minor-unit conventions; XIRR requires agreed dated cash-flow, income/fee, FX and root/no-root handling. DynamoDB transactions provide atomic operations within one account/Region, limited to 100 actions/4 MB, and their request-token idempotency window is only 10 minutes. Persistent import idempotency is an application responsibility. [DynamoDB transaction contract](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_TransactWriteItems.html)

For larger imports, evaluate a staged immutable batch with a single atomic visibility/commit marker tied to the owner-confirmed manifest and audit/outbox record. **Every** ledger reader, projection and replay consumer must enforce that marker; no partially staged row may affect holdings. Concurrent imports need a consistent owner/account version policy. Test a crash before/after each stage and repeated confirmation after a day. If these invariants or investigation queries are impractical at measured cost, compare PostgreSQL explicitly and reconcile the serverless preference in an ADR. Do not split an import across independent writes and call it atomic. S3 and DynamoDB are not one distributed transaction.

### Async jobs and continuations

Define a durable job state machine with accepted, runnable, leased/running, waiting, succeeded, failed, cancelled and needs-owner states; names are proposed, terminal semantics are required. Store stable job/task IDs, attempts, lease expiry, heartbeat, input snapshot/hash, build/config versions, timeout and reservation references. Use transactional outbox publication, duplicate-safe consumers and reconciliation for commit-to-dispatch gaps. A scheduler, queue receipt or stream is not the authoritative job state.

Before implementation choose **Lambda Durable Functions** (workflow written/checkpointed in supported Lambda application code) versus **Step Functions** (external state machine, especially useful for optional SageMaker/service coordination). Runtime, regional support, state retention, replay semantics and total costs need evidence; Python 3.12 starter compatibility cannot be assumed for Durable Functions. Queues/DLQs provide buffering and failure handling where needed; replay of side effects still requires application idempotency. External API ambiguity is recorded as unknown/pending reconciliation, not blindly retried as free. Long waits, owner approvals and larger training runs are continuations rather than one indefinitely running Lambda. [Durable runtimes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/durable-supported-runtimes.html), [Durable execution](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/durable-functions.html)

## 5. Quantitative truth and controlled learning

Data adapters preserve issuer/security/listing identities, provider symbol mapping, venue/calendar, currency/units, observation time, available/known-at time, ingest time, source version and quality. Yahoo Finance plus Twelve Data Grow is the selected source combination; coverage, personal-use rights, exact tier/quota and point-in-time history remain per-listing gates. Unsupported intraday data means labelled daily analysis and suppressed intraday alerts. Formal forecasts are daily, with 30-minute quote/risk refresh only where inputs support it.

The pipeline is reproducible source snapshot → versioned features → chronological rolling/expanding evaluation → calibration/benchmark comparison → candidate/shadow evidence → owner promotion → immutable published forecast → mature outcome and score. Fit imputation, normalization, feature selection and calibration inside training folds; purge/embargo must reflect the actual horizon and label/feature overlap. Today’s constituents, revisions or LLM extraction knowledge cannot silently enter historical folds. Record dataset/feature/model artefact hashes, parameters, seeds, split/cutoff/calendar policies, evidence references and uncertainty.

Keep separate targets for short-term horizons, 3/6/12-month forecasts and 3/5-year scenarios. Scenarios are not prematurely scored as equivalent evaluated forecasts. Do not invent mature outcomes for newly issued long-horizon predictions: distinguish backtest, historical reconstructed evidence, shadow and genuinely prospective track records. Score only after maturity against the declared canonical outcome; corrections append linked records and preserve the original published view.

Rules/statistical baselines → numerical ML → ML plus versioned LLM-derived structured features → additional approved families form an ablation ladder. An LLM may extract factors, classify exposures and propose experiments, but confident prose is not numerical calibration or an outcome label. Compare incremental quality, stability, leakage risk and cost. Exact sample sizes, thresholds, shadow duration, action formulas and rollback policy remain to agree. DEC-031 requires evidence, shadow, then owner approval; automatic promotion is excluded.

| Still-open execution option | What stays the same | Evidence needed to select |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: portable bounded ML jobs | Same data contracts, walk-forward science, immutable records and owner approval; use portable artefacts/jobs | Runtime/memory/package duration measurements, suitable job runner for work too large for Lambda, failure recovery and total operations cost |
| B: selective SageMaker training | Same science; bounded training jobs plus managed registration where justified; Lambda inference where compatible | Initial training/experimentation frequency, setup/storage/registry costs, job caps, model export compatibility and operations benefit |

Neither option is selected. Existing options documentation favours B as a proposal; this is not an owner decision or a quality advantage. Start with the cheapest evidence-producing baseline, then select the execution option after representative offline measurements and a revised total cost model. No continuously provisioned endpoint is assumed.

## 6. Research, chat, approvals and guardrails

Use a versioned specialist catalogue: market/data health, rules/performance explanation, risk/exposure, filing/news extraction, bull/bear research, briefing, model experiment proposer, evaluation/quality and orchestration roles. Exact role count is a design proposal. Each manifest defines input/output schemas, read-only tools, evidence scope, model/prompt/config versions, token/time/iteration/concurrency ceilings, purpose/environment, evaluation requirements and fallback. A role does not receive broad database or shell access because it is called an agent.

The application calls Anthropic directly through its official client SDK and explicitly controls the loop. Model-requested tools are validated, allowlisted and executed server-side; retrieved documents cannot issue privileged instructions. Numerical values come from typed deterministic tools with source IDs and freshness. Extractions carry uncertainty and citations. User-visible memory is scoped, versioned, bounded and correctable; imported source text cannot silently become a permanent instruction. Persist conversation/message IDs with client idempotency and per-conversation sequencing; final responses link to the evidence/prediction/config versions actually used. A changed holding after a chat response does not rewrite that response’s context. [Anthropic tool-use contract](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/how-tool-use-works)

Keep safety/guardrail checks, answer-quality T0/T1/T2 evaluations and numerical predictive evaluation separate. Offline deterministic cases precede bounded paid trials; online checks, sampled judges and owner calibration are metered. A language judge cannot certify profitable forecasts. Sensitive actions such as model promotion, import commit, reprocessing changes, source deletion, replay with consequences and budget changes require explicit server-verified owner authority. An authenticated chat instruction alone is not a bypass around the corresponding confirmation contract.

## 7. Costs, audit and recovery from the first useful layer

The discovery dashboard launches with dev/prod/local/shared cost views, agent/model/feature/service attribution and collector health. The confirmed envelope is **£100/month all-in**, **£70 planned + £30 reserve**; forecast cash warnings/reductions/optional-job pauses at **£60/£75/£85**. Initial A/B totals are historical examples for the initial workload, not a priced guarantee for all requirements. Include AWS, data, Claude/evals, CI/builds, storage/backups, telemetry, transfer, domain/Apple costs where applicable, FX and tax.

**Proposed admission algorithm:** atomically reserve a conservative maximum for a logical paid request/job before dispatch against a versioned budget; count parallel outstanding reservations, known liabilities and other organization credit consumption. Resolve final usage or retain liability for ambiguous responses. Dedupe retries/provider report rows and reconcile late adjustments. Environment/agent/feature/model breakdowns partition the same charge; parent/child spans do not each create additional bills. Provider reports replace/reconcile covered estimates rather than being added on top. Shared/unallocated amounts remain visible.

Live application estimates are distinct from Anthropic reports collected every **6 hours** and AWS reports every **24 hours**. Dashboard refresh reads cached aggregates; it does not query paid billing APIs. AWS Cost Explorer data can lag upstream collection; the documented API charge is per paginated request. Anthropic analytics availability, access scope and freshness must be validated for the actual account. Preserve original currency/price version and dated GBP FX/tax presentation. [AWS Cost Explorer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-what-is.html), [Anthropic analytics](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-analytics-api)

The **$200 organization credit** is user-reported and unverified, shared across environments/apps and potentially on a different reset cycle. Gross usage, credit applied, remaining verifiable credit and cash liability are separate. If coverage cannot be established, refuse uncovered Claude calls; pause optional calls when credit is low. No automatic paid fallback. Internal admission is not a universal instantaneous AWS billing cap, and stale credit information must reduce permissible discretionary work rather than fabricate headroom.

Carry business IDs plus run/trace/span/request IDs, parent/retry/replay links, environment and build/config/model versions across UI/API/jobs/tools/storage/notification. Async continuations may link separate traces. Operational retention is **logs 14 days / rich traces 30 days / run summaries 90 days**, subject to cost; durable ledger/forecast/approval/audit evidence uses a separately agreed policy and cannot disappear with trace TTL. S3 originals have **24-month renewable** retention with owner extension/deletion; no automatic expiry/deletion is authorised. Design deletion for versions, derived copies and backups with explicit tombstones/failure states, not an irreversible lock.

Monthly focused recovery/audit-integrity exercises and change-triggered checks are required. Agree RPO/RTO, exact backup retention and restore scope; prove restoration of object versions, committed records, model/prediction lineage, outbox and costs together in an isolated environment. Monitor stale schedules, queue age/DLQs, reservation leaks, failed collectors and incomplete jobs. Sensitive payloads, prompts and source documents do not belong in general telemetry; redact and minimise, with restricted evidence access. Provider-side retention is separate: calling Anthropic means selected inputs leave AWS.

# Network topology options N0 and N1

**DRAFT · MP-15 · 1 November 2026 · Technical architecture appendix · Unreviewed · No deployment or network choice approved**

This appendix makes the network alternatives explicit alongside the [system blueprint]({{page:NEW-ARCHITECTURE}}) and [technology matrix]({{page:NEW-TECH-STACK}}). It is intended as an inline companion on the MP Confluence architecture page, not a new child page or permission to publish. The current task authorises documentation and a native Lucid diagram only. Account, Region, CIDRs, AZ IDs, resource names, rules and endpoints remain unprovisioned. Full requirements and UX agreement still gate application implementation. Synthetic local/dev fixtures remain local; nothing is loaded into AWS.

## 1. N0: customer-VPC-unattached Lambda as the cost baseline candidate

N0 evaluates the app without attaching its Lambda functions to a customer VPC. Lambda still runs in AWS-managed infrastructure; “unattached” does not mean the function itself is a publicly addressable server. API Gateway is the authenticated application front door. Cognito managed sign-in, verified Apple/Google/passkey linking/recovery, object authorization, least-privilege IAM, encryption and environment isolation are still required.

Use direct outbound TLS from the bounded Lambda workers for Anthropic's API, Yahoo Finance and Twelve Data Grow. The application owns the official Anthropic client SDK loop, read-only tool allowlists, URL/redirect validation, token/time/iteration ceilings and cost admission. An application URL allowlist is not the same control as a network firewall. No Bedrock, AgentCore or Agent SDK runtime is introduced. AWS explains that default Lambda networking has internet access, while a function attached to a customer VPC needs an explicit egress path. [Lambda internet access](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/internet-access-lambda-function)

CloudFront and Route 53 serve the web entry point. If the static SvelteKit option is selected, a standard private S3 origin uses signed OAC and a distribution-scoped bucket policy, with Block Public Access and encryption. S3 website endpoints do not support this OAC design. OAC protects the origin, not the confidentiality of every viewer response: holdings, imports, chat and cost data must not be baked into static assets or publicly cached. Dynamic SSR remains a separate, unselected adapter/runtime/session decision. [S3 origin protection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html)

N0 accesses S3/DynamoDB through their managed service APIs using IAM/TLS; it has no customer subnet, gateway endpoint, NAT or customer security group. Data buckets/tables remain private by policy. Neither a customer VPC nor a VPN is required simply to make the product owner-only. Public TLS endpoints still require authentication, throttling and application security; a private API/VPN design is a separately costed alternative, not the baseline.

## 2. N1: optional split topology with a private VPC scope

N1 adds a customer VPC only for a demonstrated private-resource or compute-isolation need. It does not attach every internet-facing worker by default. Keep the direct Anthropic/retrieval/market-data functions customer-VPC-unattached; place only justified private jobs or VPC attachments in two isolated private subnets across two AZs. This is a candidate design, not a selected infrastructure plan or an availability guarantee.

Lambda execution remains in the Lambda service. A VPC-configured Lambda uses Hyperplane ENIs to reach the customer network; the diagram distinguishes those attachment interfaces from the service's execution infrastructure. Optional Fargate/SageMaker job networking must be evaluated for the selected execution mode. Two AZs do not turn a single job, a regional dependency or a backup into a multi-region recovery design. [Lambda VPC attachment](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/using-aws-lambda-iam-condition-keys-for-vpc-settings/)

| Component | Proposed N1 contract | Deliberately absent/unselected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer VPC | CIDR/DNS settings to agree; dev/prod separation under the environment ADR | No inherited MA network/account/Region |
| Private subnet A/B | One isolated subnet per AZ; no public addresses assigned to Lambda; route tables associated explicitly | No default internet route in this split candidate |
| Route tables | VPC local route; same-Region S3/DynamoDB service-prefix routes to gateway endpoints | No claim that an S3 gateway reaches Anthropic, arbitrary URLs or another VPC |
| Workload security group | No unsolicited inbound rules; narrowly scoped role-specific egress, such as required TCP443 service prefixes; application/database inbound only for a separately justified dependency | No shared “allow everything” group; not an HTTP hostname/DNS firewall |
| Gateway endpoints | S3 and DynamoDB route targets, associated with both selected subnet route tables; scoped endpoint policies | Not interface endpoint ENIs and not a reason to put S3/DynamoDB inside the VPC |
| AWS managed services | S3, DynamoDB, Cognito, API Gateway and CloudFront remain outside the customer VPC boundary | They are not deployed into the two private subnets |
| External API roles | Separate unattached Lambda functions retain outbound internet access without customer NAT | No direct inbound path into private subnets from the public API inferred |
| API invocation | AWS service integration invokes an authorized Lambda; private job dispatch/state follows the durable workflow contract | API Gateway invocation is not an inbound socket opened on a Lambda ENI |

Gateway endpoints support their named service in the selected Region; their route and policy scope must match actual access. They have no additional endpoint charge, but the S3/DynamoDB service, requests, storage, backups and compute are still billed. Evaluate DNS resolution, service-prefix routes, network ACL return paths, IAM and endpoint policies together. [S3 gateway endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html), [DynamoDB gateway endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-ddb.html)

Security groups allow traffic by protocol, port, addresses/prefix lists and security-group references; they do not restrict destinations by DNS name. They also cannot block queries to AmazonProvidedDNS/Route 53 Resolver. DNS Firewall or an inspected proxy/firewall would be additional controls with their own coverage and cost decisions, not a capability hidden inside an SG. [Security-group rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-group-rules.html)

## 3. N1-E: conditional public egress if all workers must be VPC-attached

This is an **unselected change to N1**, shown separately so the additional resources and route changes are visible. For classic zonal public NAT, each participating AZ has a public subnet/NAT gateway, the public route table sends `0.0.0.0/0` to an attached internet gateway, and the private subnet's default route points to its same-AZ NAT. Permit only necessary workload egress; NAT itself is connectivity, not destination authorization. Retain the more-specific S3/DynamoDB gateway routes for those services.

Putting Lambda in a public subnet does **not** give it a public IP or internet access. Likewise, an IGW alone does not give a private Lambda ENI an outbound IPv4 path. Do not draw a direct private-subnet-to-IGW shortcut. A one-NAT design may reduce fixed cost but adds an AZ dependency and potentially cross-AZ transfer; two zonal NATs avoid that specific cross-AZ dependency while increasing the monthly floor. Other NAT products/IPv6 strategies require a new compatibility/pricing comparison, not an assumed free equivalent. [Lambda egress requirements](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/internet-access-lambda-function), [NAT placement/cost](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-pricing.html)

## 4. Optional private-job service reachability and paid endpoints

Do not assume an isolated subnet can launch every training/container workload using just an S3 gateway. Record a call-by-call dependency matrix for build/pull, start, runtime tools, logging, model/data access, callbacks, cancellation and recovery. A container image pull, a job's training data path and a model API call are different routes.

- For Fargate/ECR workloads without internet, verify both `ecr.api` and `ecr.dkr` interface endpoints, S3 layer access and CloudWatch Logs access for the selected platform/log driver. Other runtime API calls can need additional endpoints. [ECS endpoint considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/vpc-endpoints.html)
- Regional STS is needed only where the actual code/service path calls STS through that network; add KMS or other service endpoints only where the selected runtime uses their APIs. Do not assume every endpoint is mandatory or that all services share one endpoint.
- SageMaker service-side download/logging and a training container's own networking differ, particularly with network isolation. Validate the chosen job's VPC configuration and service-side paths rather than copying the Fargate endpoint list. With network isolation the container cannot freely call the internet or private resources. [SageMaker VPC/network isolation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/interface-vpc-endpoint.html)
- Each interface endpoint requires service/Region/DNS/endpoint-policy compatibility and an endpoint SG permitting the intended workload SG on the required port. Those endpoint SGs are distinct from the route-based S3/DynamoDB gateway endpoints. New endpoint/logging/control-plane costs require the budget gate.

ML option A portable jobs versus B selective SageMaker remains unselected. The diagram's private-job interfaces and optional paid endpoint box describe capabilities to investigate, not approved Fargate/SageMaker activation or an always-on inference endpoint.

## 5. Policies must preserve every legitimate access path

Keep separate service/role paths for CloudFront OAC web assets, unattached Lambda data access, optional VPC jobs through gateway endpoints, confirmed owner upload/read URLs, CI/deployment and approved recovery tools. Scope each to the required objects/actions/environment and audit it. The static web origin and sensitive raw archive need different viewer/access policies.

A blanket bucket/table deny requiring `aws:SourceVpce` can break CloudFront, unattached workers, console/CI or restoration. AWS's S3 endpoint examples explicitly warn about blocking non-endpoint access. Design resource and endpoint policies together, with narrowly justified principal/service exceptions or separate resources rather than pasting a global deny. A network path does not replace IAM authorization, and an endpoint policy does not grant an otherwise unauthorized principal access. [S3 endpoint policy considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

## 6. Cost comparison and decision gate

The confirmed envelope remains **£100 monthly cash all-in**, **£70 operation + £30 reserve**, covering dev/prod, data, Claude/evaluations and operating overhead. No suballocation proves that a VPC/NAT design fits. The shared $200 Anthropic credit is user-reported/unverified and does not offset unrelated AWS networking charges.

| Cost class | Planning formula; Region/rate/tax/FX remain to verify | Implication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| N0 customer-network fixed floor | No customer NAT/interface endpoints introduced by N0 | App, requests, transfer, edge, identity, storage, telemetry and recovery still cost money |
| S3/DynamoDB gateway endpoints | No additional endpoint hourly/data-processing charge | Not a free storage/compute guarantee; only named service routes |
| Classic zonal public NAT | `number of NATs × provisioned hours × regional NAT hourly rate + processed GB × rate + applicable transfer/IPv4 charges` | Idle gateways still incur fixed cost; two AZs can double the gateway-hour floor |
| Interface endpoints | Sum over required services/AZs: `provisioned endpoint-AZ hours × regional rate + processed GB × rate` | An ECR/logging/STS/etc. endpoint portfolio can cost substantially more than one endpoint |
| Flow/DNS/firewall/edge logs | Measured ingestion, storage, queries, rules/requests and retention | Monitoring the network is separately budgeted; sensitive logs need restricted encrypted storage |

AWS prices NAT by provisioned hour plus processed data and applicable transfer, and PrivateLink by endpoint-AZ-hour plus processed data. The [VPC pricing page](https://aws.amazon.com/vpc/pricing/) currently illustrates **$0.045/hour** for its **US East (Ohio)** NAT example: 730 illustrative hours gives **$32.85 for one gateway's hours alone**, before data, applicable IPv4/transfer, tax and GBP conversion. Two at that example rate would be $65.70 for gateway hours alone. **This is not a quote for the unselected project Region or a complete bill.** The fixed floor can threaten the available AWS portion of the all-in budget even with low traffic. [PrivateLink pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/privatelink/pricing/)

Provisional evaluation order: measure N0 as the cost baseline, identify an actual private dependency, then compare the smallest N1 split that addresses it; evaluate N1-E only if all-worker VPC attachment is a requirement. The owner selects the network option after evidence. Neither security nor cost is established merely by adding a VPC icon.

Before implementation approval, record the N0/N1 ADR, full-scope regional cost comparison, complete service/path policy matrix, two-AZ/route/endpoint failure cases, authenticated SSE/adapter proof, endpoint/job bootstrap evidence, source/credit collector behavior, recovery access and source/data deletion controls. This task does not perform cloud connectivity tests, pricing-account calls, policy deployment or independent review.

## 3. Compatibility facts checked against primary sources

- **SvelteKit 3 is available.** The [official announcement](https://svelte.dev/blog/sveltekit-3-is-here) is dated 1 October 2026; the [migration guide](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/migrating-to-sveltekit-3) covers its breaking changes. No SvelteKit version is currently installed in this product. Select a compatible exact Svelte/Kit/Vite/Node/adapter set with a lock when the build is authorised; do not substitute historical Svelte 3 for SvelteKit 3.
- **Static and SSR differ.** [SvelteKit static adapter](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/adapter-static) produces static files. Dynamic server logic needs another adapter/runtime; Cognito client sign-in alone does not create server-side SvelteKit sessions.
- **SSE is a constrained AWS integration.** [API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/response-transfer-mode.html) documents REST proxy response streaming and a 15-minute ceiling. [Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-response-streaming.html) documents Python custom runtime/Web Adapter requirements and billed continuation after disconnect. Region availability and the complete authenticated Python path still need validation.
- **Workflow runtime matters.** [Durable Functions’ supported runtimes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/durable-supported-runtimes.html) include Python 3.13/3.14 at this check; the starter CI’s Python 3.12 is not sufficient evidence for that choice. Step Functions remains the external state-machine alternative; neither is activated or selected here.
- **Financial atomicity has real bounds.** [DynamoDB transactions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_TransactWriteItems.html) have action/size/idempotency limits. A staged immutable import with consistent commit visibility or an explicit relational alternative needs proof before design approval.
- **Cognito features do not prove a complete recovery design.** [Authentication flows](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/amazon-cognito-user-pools-authentication-flow-methods.html) describe federation/passkeys; [federated linking](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-identity-federation-consolidate-users.html) is a privileged identity operation. Validate tier, canonical local owner, linking, recovery and reauthentication as one flow; do not grant access on email equality.

Permission/response/API version checks remain future implementation evidence.

These are planning controls, not an instant universal AWS billing cap or verified funded service allocation.
- Claude: the reported $200 organization credit is unverified and shared, not multiplied per environment. Track gross usage, credit and cash separately; pause optional calls when low and refuse uncovered/unverifiable calls. No automatic paid fallback.
- Dashboard: cost visibility on the main app at launch; dev/prod/local/shared and agent/model/feature/service attribution. Live internal estimates differ from delayed provider reports. Anthropic collection is six-hourly and AWS daily, with cached refreshes and collector freshness/health. No collector or account permission has been configured by this work.
- Identity: Cognito managed sign-in with Apple/Google/passkeys and proof-based linking; two independent passkey recovery paths. Tier, sessions, reauthentication, recovery and revocation still need validation. No auth resources are provisioned.
- Originals: encrypted private S3 archive, renewable 24-month default and owner extension/deletion controls. No automatic deletion is authorised. Required ledger/forecast/approval/audit lineage has a separate retention policy, still to specify.
- Operational telemetry: 14-day logs, 30-day rich traces and 90-day run summaries, subject to measured cost. Sampling/TTLs never replace required durable source/financial evidence.
- Recovery: monthly focused recovery/audit-integrity exercises plus checks after relevant changes. RPO/RTO, backup windows, deletion completion and exact scenarios remain pending; no cloud job is configured.
